source.title: ConsistentFeature: A Plug-and-Play Component for Neural Network Regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material text supplied; no truncation affecting the relevant experiment.
record.tranche_reason: Tests memorization on randomized labels using a different regularization-comparison setup, reporting training-loss behavior for ResNet18 on Flower102-Random.
record.gate_note: The paper's general discussion of Zhang et al. is cited prior work, not a result row. Its own relevant result is the ResNet18 Flower102-Random comparison in Section 4.4/Figure 5 and Appendix Figure 8; the supplied text describes it but gives no numerical training-loss values. The paper does not report zero training error or chance test error for the unregularized baseline.
record.test_reason: The study trains ResNet18 on randomly relabeled Flower102 and measures training loss and accuracy, directly testing random-label fitting and its sensitivity to dropout and weight decay. The supplied text lacks readable endpoints establishing perfect fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that CF strongly suppresses memorization while promoting real-data convergence and generalization; label smoothing barely suppresses memorization, dropout has limited suppression even at 0.8, and weight decay harms real-data generalization in this comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random labels to compare regularization methods' memorization suppression, following the cited Arpit et al. setup; it does not provide the original source's numerical fit-to-random-label result. The experiment uses ResNet18 on Flower102 and reports qualitative comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization method changes the reported memorization suppression and real-data generalization outcomes; Dropout's stated memorization result is for rate 0.8.

fits_no_version.finding: CF almost entirely suppresses random-label fitting while improving real-data validation loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An added adversarial feature-consistency regularizer can suppress memorization while preserving or improving real-data generalization.

record.problems: Relevant random-label results are mainly qualitative in the supplied text; figure curves are not numerically described. The text does not state the baseline's final training error, chance-level test error, or detailed sample/replicate counts for this comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 5 is described in text but its plotted numerical values are not available in the supplied text; Appendix Figure 8 is a figure-only training-accuracy comparison.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error is not reported. Identical architecture and training hyperparameters across clean and random labeling are not fully documented.
No quantified clean-versus-random fitting-time comparison or corruption-fraction convergence sweep.
No shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No controlled corruption-fraction sweep measuring both perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance.
Data augmentation is not tested in the random-label comparison. Good generalization after removing all named regularizers is not established.
The real-patterns-before-memorization sequence is attributed to prior research, not demonstrated by this study's own results.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is warranted on the versions' full fitting or generalization endpoints from the supplied qualitative statements alone. Missing endpoint information is not a scope limitation or a challenge. Figure-only accuracy results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not added to missing. Section 4.4's Figure 10j/k references appear inconsistent with Figure 10's caption; Figure 5 and Figure 8 concern the relevant experiment.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the unregularized baseline's numerical training error, whether it reaches zero or near-zero, or test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed against true-label training.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep from clean labels through increasing corruption fractions to fully random labels.

Tests dropout and weight decay against a random-label memorization outcome, but does not test data augmentation in this comparison or whether removing regularizers alone harms true-label generalization.
Does not report a training-time sequence showing real patterns learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Flower102-Random, created by assigning random labels to each training sample; the text describes training-loss curves.

conditions.value: randomly assigned to each training sample

rows.value: The baseline is shown in the training-loss comparison; no value is stated in the text.
rows.note: No numeric baseline training error or explicit statement that the baseline reaches zero is supplied.
rows.check: No baseline training-loss or accuracy endpoint is readable. 'None' should mean no added comparison regularizer: the default optimizer is AdamW, whose weight-decay setting is unspecified.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Flower102-Random with dropout; the text says it has limited memorization suppression, even at dropout rate 0.8.
rows.value: Limited ability to suppress model memorization, even at a dropout rate of 0.8.
rows.note: The stated result concerns dropout's limited suppression on random labels; no numerical training error is given.
rows.check: Limited suppression establishes continued memorization, but does not establish zero or near-zero training error, or demonstrate incomplete fitting. The original partial state confuses suppression strength with fitting completeness.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Flower102-Random with weight decay.
rows.value: Weight Decay overly restricts the model’s search space, leading to reduced generalization on real data.
rows.note: The text does not explicitly state the random-label training-loss outcome for Weight Decay.
rows.check: The recorded value concerns real-data generalization, not this row's random-label training outcome. Replace it with a readable random-label result if available; the supplied text provides none.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.value: LabelSmoothing has almost no memory suppression ability on random data.
rows.note: The text explicitly characterizes memory suppression as almost absent; no numeric training error is given.
rows.check: Label smoothing is outside V5's named regularizers. Almost no suppression indicates memorization persists, but does not establish the near-perfect fitting required by V1.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on standard Flower102 with the same settings used for the random-data comparison.
rows.note: The stated conclusion concerns weight decay; no numerical validation-loss values are included in the supplied description.
rows.check: Reduced generalization with weight decay bears on its necessity, but the comparison baseline and its absolute generalization are unspecified. This is not evidence challenging V5.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on standard Flower102 with the same settings used for the random-data comparison.
rows.value: Dropout has minimal effect on real data performance.
rows.note: No numerical real-data performance value is stated.
rows.check: Minimal performance change with dropout bears on its necessity, but does not establish that generalization without it is good; baseline performance is unspecified.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.value: CF suppresses the model’s fitting (memory behavior) on noisy data almost entirely.
rows.note: The authors state the qualitative result but provide no numerical training error in the text.
rows.check: CF adds a discriminator and a new adversarial training objective specifically to suppress memorization. Its success does not test V1's unchanged training setup or V5's named regularizers. The original observed state describes suppression, not the claimed fitting effect.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on standard Flower102 with CF under the same setup as the random-data experiment.
rows.value: CF enhances generalization ability on real data, resulting in the lowest validation loss.
rows.note: The statement is qualitative; no baseline or numerical validation-loss values are stated.
rows.check: Improved validation loss with CF measures the proposed method's performance, not random-label fitting or removal of V5's named regularizers.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The paper identifies training-loss curves but gives no text-reported baseline value establishing zero or near-zero error (R1).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 on Flower102-Random with CF, Dropout, or LabelSmoothing

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 on standard Flower102 with Weight Decay or Dropout
reader_labels.reason: The text says Weight Decay reduces real-data generalization and Dropout has minimal effect on real-data performance, so regularizer behavior depends on method (R5, R6).
